name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz ~65% below pre-war; mine claims 13–14 Nov
summary: Iran says three tankers hit mines near Hormuz on 14 Nov; traffic about 65% below pre-war levels (UKMTO)
state: Iranian state TV said on 14 Nov that three oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire, two inside the Strait of Hormuz and one east of it, and warned ships using routes without Iranian approval (AP). The IRGC made a similar claim about a gas tanker on 13 Nov (Al Jazeera); the claims are unverified. UKMTO put Hormuz traffic about 65% below pre-conflict levels in the week to 10 Nov, with JMIC rating the threat severe (Gulf News). Materially impeded Hormuz traffic sets the Alert.
for_you: Shipping, energy and fertiliser supply chains that rely on the Gulf face delays, rerouting and higher insurance and freight costs, which tend to feed through to fuel and goods prices. Seafarers and operators should follow UKMTO and flag-state guidance.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded: ~65% below pre-conflict levels (UKMTO, week to 10 Nov)

Al Jazeera — IRGC says tanker caught fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
